name: CoastMath: FIRE Calculator
dev: Blank Slate Labs Limited Liability Company

ios.desc:
CoastMath projects your finances year by year, so you can see when you can stop working and what every year after that looks like.

Enter your accounts, income, expenses, homes, debts and milestones. CoastMath projects net worth, cash flow and taxes for every year of your plan.

PLAN
• Overview: net worth by year, the cash flow of any year, milestones and taxes over time
• Year detail: income, spending, withdrawals, contributions and taxes, item by item
• Income, Expenses and Accounts tabs with monthly or annual amounts
• Social Security estimates, savings rules and a drawdown order
• Federal, state and local income taxes, RMDs and health coverage
• Advanced: milestones, assumptions and household details

ANALYZE
• Chance of success from Monte Carlo trials
• Stress tests: historical periods, a market crash or a job loss
• Withdrawal rules compared with your planned spending
• Tax strategies: Roth conversions and gain harvesting that fill a bracket
• Tax suggestions and SEPP 72(t) early withdrawals
• Compare plans, track your actual net worth and read the annual report

Explore a read-only sample plan without an account, or sign in with Apple, Google or an email link to save your own plans.

FREE AND PREMIUM
Every planning feature is free. Free includes one plan, editable for 7 days after you create it; its projection keeps updating after that.

CoastMath Premium keeps every plan editable and adds unlimited plans, plan duplication, restoring archived plans, and CSV, PDF and JSON exports of the annual report. Premium is $29.99 per month or $99.99 per year, charged to your Apple Account. It renews automatically unless canceled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Manage or cancel it in your Apple Account settings.

Balances are entered manually; bank connections are not included. Projections are calculated on CoastMath's servers and need an internet connection.

Projections are hypothetical estimates based on your inputs and assumptions, not financial, tax or legal advice.

Terms of use: https://coastmath.com/terms

Privacy policy: https://coastmath.com/privacy

quotes.text:
Self-hosting instructions in the README.

Hosted version: https://coastmath.com/

iOS app: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6809539979

This post is partially inspired by this thread: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50048344

```
> Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt.

>> No, they can't, at least not any semblance of quality. The cases we're seeing where this does kinda work is in ports and translation where all the rules are already documented in the best specification language possible with a way for the LLM to verify itself: code. We saw this close to a year ago now with Cloudflare and NextJS
```

This post mostly outlines how I am personally building with agents, as I am almost entirely hands-off.

Desired feature-set determined by having agents research existing products and feedback / feature requests on FIRE subreddits.

Features built using Opus 5.5 (xhigh) / Fable 5.1 (med/high) as orchestrator and Opus-5-5 low/medium as worker subagents.

Quality is attempted by running Opus-5-5 agents in a perpetual audit + fixer loop on the calculation / compliance engine until no medium+ severity can be found. The origin of each rule / logic must be backed up and documented in the codebase with a source.
